EDITORS
                                                Mustafa Turğut

He received his BA degree from Boğaziçi University, Sociology Department in 2003; his MA degree from Fırat
University Sociology Department in 2007 with the thesis on the topic of modernization and nationalism en-
titled 'Türk Ulusal Basınında Milliyetçi ve Modernist İmge İnşası: Yurtdışında Yaşayan Türklere Dair Başarı Haberl-
eri' (Nationalist and Modernist Imagery Construction in Turkish National Press: Success Stories about Turkish
People Living Abroad). Since 2009 he continues his PhD studies in Middle East Technical University at the
sociology department, on the topic of Turkish family structure. Between the years of 2006-2010 he worked as
assistant specialist at T.R. Ministry of Family and Social Policies, Department of Research and Policies. Working
as a specialist, he conducted 11 researches, operated as a coordinator for 3 training development projects and
as a member of monitoring and appraisal team between the years of 2011-2012. Since 2013 he works as head
of department of Research and Policies at the Ministry of Family and Social Policies.

                                               Semiha Feyzioğlu

She received her BA degree from Marmara University on Political Science and International Affairs Depart-
ment in 2004; and her MA degree from Sabancı University on European Studies in 2005. She has been working
as researcher since 2006; and currently is a group leader in Ipsos Social Research Institute. She has directed
various social research projects such as “Türkiye's Fertility Rates Fall, Potential Impacts and Proactive Policy
Recommendations”, and “Single Parents in Türkiye” for the Ministry of Family and Social Policies; “Youth and
Social Media” and “Young Authors Story Contest Profile and Content Analysis” for the Ministry of Youth and
Sports; “the Evaluation of Social Support Programme” for the Ministry of Development; and " Domestic Vio-
lence and Child Abuse " for UNICEF.



                                         CONTRIBUTORS
                                              Dr. Ayşe İdil Aybars

Ayşe Idil Aybars is Assistant Professor at the Middle East Technical University (METU), Department of So-
ciology and Social Policy Program. She has her BSc and MSc degrees at METU Department of Sociology.
She completed an MSc degree in European Studies at the London School of Economics and Political Sci-
ence (LSE) in 2002, and a Ph.D. degree in Social Sciences at the University of Ulster in 2007. She worked as
Postdoctoral Research Fellow at METU Center for European Studies between 2006 and 2009, where she
took part in numerous research, infrastructure and network projects funded by the EU and other fund-
ing bodies. She was a Max Weber Fellow at the European University Institute (EUI) in Italy in 2009-2010.
Her research interests include comparative social policy analysis, gender equality in employment and
education, EU social policy and sociology of media and communications. She has also acted as consult-
ant and researcher in various projects concerning social policy, development targets, gender equality,
child wellbeing, early childhood education and care, women’s employment, women with disabilities and
children’s rights with UNICEF, UNDP, UNFPA, World Bank and European Parliament.
                                                                                                  Contributors   5



                                        Dr. Fatma Umut Beşpınar

Dr. Beşpınar is an assistant professor of sociology at the Middle East Technical University in Ankara, Türki-
ye (Ph.D. in Sociology, University of Texas at Austin, 2007; MA in Sociology, Middle East Technical Univer-
sity, 2001; BS in Sociology, Middle East Technical University, 1998). Her areas of interest are social policy,
family, gender and migration. She has published chapters in edited volumes such as Women in the Mid-
dle East and North Africa: Agents of Change; Routledge Handbook of Modern Türkiye; Migration, Family
and Social Position: Contributions to Education, Gender and Care Dynamics; Türkiye and the Politics of
National Identity: Social, Economic and Cultural Transformation, articles in such journals Women Studies
International Forum and national and international agencies’ reports, namely “Child Well-Being in Early
Years and Women’s Employment Policy Paper” for the Ministry of Family and Social Policy and UNICEF,
“Single Parents in Türkiye” for the Ministry of Family and Social Policies, “An Analysis of the Demand for
Different Forms of Human Trafficking in Türkiye” for the International Organization for Migration.

                                      Assoc. Prof. Dr. Alanur Çavlin

Received her bachelors degree from Sociology Department of Middle East Technical University (1999)
and her PHD from Hacettepe University Institute of Population Studies (2007). She received post-doc-
toral fellowships from Queens University Sociology Department Surveillance Studies Center (2009-2011)
with her Project on surveillance of the transformation of population intelligence systems, and from Tür-
kiye Science Academy (2007-2009) with her Project on analysing population censuses in Türkiye with its
societal, political and economic aspects. She worked as visiting professor in the Sociology Departments
of the Middle East Technical University and Queens University (2007-2011). She continues her academic
studies on fertility and contraception with a focus on gender relationships and ethnic diversity; and on
censuses and registration systems with a focus on surveillance, neoliberalism and citizenship at Hac-
ettepe University Institute of Population Studies.

                                   Assoc. Prof. Dr. Mehmet Ali Eryurt

He was graduated from the Sociology Department of the Middle East Technical University in 1999. He
received his MA and PHD degrees from the Hacettepe University Institute of Population Studies, and re-
ceived his Associate Professor degree in 2013 in the area of Demography. He is currently working at the
Hacettepe University Institute of Population Studies. He has contributed to various large scale research
projects such as: Türkiye Health and Population Studies 1998, 2003, 2008 and 2013; National Maternal
Mortality Study, Migration and Deported Populations Study, Research on Domestic Violence Against
Women. He has published books, chapters and articles on topics such as the demographic transition
of Türkiye, population policies, fertility, migration and urbanization, infant mortality, child poverty and
elderly studies.
6   TAYA Findings, and Recommendations



                                            Prof. Dr. İsmet Koç

He received his bachelor’s degree from the Sociology Department of Hacettepe University in 1988, and
received his PHD on Economic and Social Demography from Hacettepe University Institute of Popula-
tion Studies in 1997. He is currently the Head of the Department of Technical Demography at the Insti-
tute of Population Studies of Hacettepe University. He has various national and international articles,
books, research and publications on topics like population and development, population policies, family
demography and research methods. His works include research projects such as; Türkiye Health and
Population Studies, Research on Violence Against Women in Türkiye, National Maternal Mortality Study,
Türkiye Migration and Deported Populations Study, and Project on BEI Approach in Shanty Towns and
Forming Public Opinion in Türkiye.

                                         Prof. Dr. Ferhunde Özbay

Prof. Dr. Ferhunde Özbay (1944) studied social services in Ankara Social Services Academy (now Hac-
ettepe University) between 1962-1966, demography in Hacettepe University in 1968-1969 and in Prince-
ton University in 1969-1970, and sociology in Cornell University between 1970 and 1975. She started
working at Bosporus University in 1982 and she was retired from the same university in 2006. She is
still working as a part time faculty member at the Department of Sociology in Bosporus University. She
wrote several articles on women’s labor, family and population in various journals and books. She edited
two books. Her articles on gender and population include; "Development of Studies on Women in Tür-
kiye", Women, Family and Social Change in Türkiye (1990); “Family and Household Structure in Türkiye:
Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow”. Women and Men in 75 Years (1998); “Gendered Space: A New Look at
Turkish Modernisation“ Gender & History (2000); “Nation-state, Population Nation-State, Surveillance
and Population Registration Systems in Türkiye”, Society ve Science (2010); “Transition of Household
Labor in Türkiye”, From Past to Today: Women Labor in Türkiye (2012).

Table 1. Classification and Definition of Family Structures Used in the Study
 Family Structure                      Definition
 1. Nuclear                                     Type of family made up of a husband-wife and/or unmarried children.
 1.1.Nuclear without children                   Type of family made up of only the husband and wife.
     1.1.1.Nuclear without children (<45 age) Type of family made up of only the husband and wife where the wife is younger than 45 years of age.
 1.1.2. Nuclear without children (≥45 age) Type of family made up of only the husband and wife where the wife is at or over 45 years of age.
 1.2.Nuclear with children                      Type of family made up of husband, wife and unmarried children.
           1.2.1.Nuclear with children-1 child Type of family made up of husband, wife and one unmarried child.
       1.2.2. Nuclear with children -2 children Type of family made up of husband, wife and two unmarried children.
     1.2.3. Nuclear with children -3+ children Type of family made up of husband, wife and three unmarried children.
 2.Extended                                     Type of family where another person or another family is added to the nuclear family unit horizontally or verti-
                                                cally.
 2.1.Patriarchal extended                       Type of family where another one or more families are added to the nuclear family unit horizontally or vertically.
 2.2.Transient extended                         Type of family where another person from a broken family or just another person is added to the nuclear family unit
                                                horizontally or vertically.
 3.Broken                                       Type of family where the nuclear family unit is reduced to one person or one parent or a family made up of
                                                individuals who may or may not be related.
 3.1.One person                                 Type of family where an adult female or an adult male lives alone.
                      3.1.1.One person-Male Type of family where an adult male lives alone.
                    3.1.2. One person-Female Type of family where an adult female lives alone.
 3.2.Single parent                              Type of family where one of the parents has split from the nuclear family with children by divorce, separation or death.
                     3.2.1.Single parent-Male Type of family where the woman has split from the nuclear family with children by divorce, separation or death.
                  3.2.2. Single parent-Female Type of family where the man has split from the nuclear family with children by divorce, separation or death.
 3.3.Other broken                               Type of family where one of the nuclear elements of a transient extended family has broken away from the family
                                                (grandmother-grandchild; grandfather-grandchild etc.).
 3.4.Non-relatives                              Type of family where members have no relationship either by blood or by kinship.
